Strong case studies demonstrating real biological impact with quantifiable improvements (21% more cell-disease associations, 13.8% higher eQTL enrichment) and validated discoveries
Thorough ablation studies systematically evaluating contribution of each component (knowledge trees, Bayesian updates, diagnostics, domain knowledge)
Excellent reproducibility with extensive appendices containing prompts, setup details, hyperparameters, and code release promised
Well-motivated problem addressing genuine bottleneck in computational method development with clear practical importance
Sensible system design integrating domain knowledge, iterative optimization with Bayesian updates, and diagnostic feedback for scientific discovery
weaknesses: Baseline fairness concerns: Biomni/ChatGPT-Agent limited to 1 hour/iteration while TusoAI has 8 hours; AIDE crashed when timeout extended—makes performance claims somewhat unfair

Ablation study O contradicts core claims: domain knowledge importance appears modest (0 vs 10 vs 50 papers show similar performance), undermining the stated importance of literature integration

Methodological questions: arbitrary time/bug-fix limits (10 min, 4 fixes); diversity selection criterion (0.1%) lacks justification; heuristic choices throughout (code similarity clustering, 'most promising' selection)

System limitations: only operates on single functions; requires separate validation set; cannot modify evaluation procedures; LLM API dependencies and version specificity limit reproducibility

Strong reproducibility with released code, detailed implementation, and prompt templates

Non-equivalent baseline comparisons: Biomni and ChatGPT-Agent evaluated non-iteratively due to web interface constraints; cannot compare with most similar concurrent work (Aygun et al. 2025) due to code unavailability

Incomplete ablations: missing ablations on Bayesian update rule (why 1.1×?), instruction vs. diagnostic split (80/20), and knowledge tree structure itself
Statistical analysis: single-cell CIs not shown ('all under 0.01'), only 3 random seeds, no formal significance testing; some individual improvements are modest

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine bottleneck in scientific method development; existing systems focus on data analysis or general ML without domain-specific integration

Thoughtful system design with three key innovations: (1) knowledge tree for structured domain knowledge, (2) hierarchical planning with Bayesian utility updates, (3) diagnostic-based optimization pathway

Comprehensive evaluation: 11 tasks with consistent outperformance (avg rank 1.2 for single-cell, 2.8 for deep learning); strong baselines including AIDE (MLE agent), Biomni, ChatGPT-Agent, and expert methods

Demonstrated real scientific impact beyond benchmarks: scDRS improvements (40% power increase, 21% more true associations) uncovered 9 new T cell-disease associations; pgBoost improvements (13.8% enrichment) discovered 7 novel variant-gene links validated against literature
Excellent reproducibility: detailed experimental setups, complete prompt templates, runtime analysis showing efficiency, code diversity analysis (TusoAI vs AIDE), and stability across replicates
Strong ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrating contribution of each component; code diversity analysis revealing TusoAI explores solution space more thoroughly than AIDE
Practical robustness: works across multiple LLMs (GPT-4o-mini to GPT-5); interestingly, cheaper models sometimes outperform expensive ones; includes warm-start capability for existing methods
Clear presentation with informative visualizations; Algorithm 1 clearly specified; extensive appendices providing transparency and supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for design choices: Bayesian update rule (πc ← 1.1πc) appears heuristic without principled justification for the multiplicative factor or adaptive alternatives

Significant applicability constraints: requires single-function optimization (fails on scattered codebases), needs separate validation experiment, vulnerable to weak evaluation functions, cannot optimize data selection or evaluation procedures themselves

Baseline comparison concerns: Biomni/ChatGPT-Agent were designed for data analysis (not method development), making comparisons somewhat unfair; deep learning baselines receive only 10 non-iterative attempts vs TusoAI's 8-hour iteration; missing direct comparison with concurrent Aygun et al. (2025) work
Domain coverage limited despite generality claims: all 6 single-cell tasks are biology, 4 of 5 deep learning tasks have biological applications; generalization beyond biology undemonstrated

Case study design raises questions about discovery vs. refinement: scDRS optimization targets region where scDRS has 'lower power' (task-specific tuning); pgBoost instructions explicitly guide toward distance-based features (guided refinement rather than autonomous discovery)

Statistical rigor concerns: some reported improvements are marginal (Table 2: TusoAI 0.70 vs Expert 0.69); no formal significance testing; knowledge source limited to top 10 citation-ranked papers (may miss recent specialized work)

Reproducibility of LLM components: multiple stochastic elements in instruction generation; generated instructions often generic across tasks (Appendix C shows repeated patterns); limited sensitivity analysis to prompt engineering

Missing failure analysis: insufficient discussion of task types/domains where TusoAI struggles; no analysis of when domain knowledge might be misleading; no examination of ill-specified evaluation function effects

Novelty of discovered methods somewhat overstated: many are combinations of known techniques (preprocessing, loss functions, ensembling); Appendix H's novelty defense sometimes just distinguishes from prior work rather than proving fundamental innovation
